accuracy.evidence: The lab and lesson follow the standard KS3 and GCSE rules checked against AQA Maths P8, BBC Bitesize KS3 tree diagrams, Corbettmaths tree-diagram practice and CCSS 7.SP.8: branches from one point add to 1; multiply along a path for a combined event; add the ends of every path that fits; with replacement the second pick stays 3/5 and 2/5; without replacement, after eating a red from 3 red and 2 blue the next is 2/4. The arithmetic is exact: 3/5 × 3/5 = 9/25 = 0.36, 6/25 + 6/25 = 12/25, 3/5 × 2/4 = 3/10. The 200-pick test is a seeded simulation that always returns 72 red-red pairs, which is 36 percent.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: adding first and second outcomes instead of multiplying (prediction 2 + 3 versus 2 × 3, and the challenge item on a coin and a dice); adding along a path (the 3/5 + 3/5 button is refused because 6/5 is greater than 1); using the part-to-part ratio 3/2 as a probability (that tile is refused with 'red is 3 of 5'); counting only one mixed path (the same-colour leaves are refused and the challenge onepath slip names both orders); keeping the old denominator after not replacing (3/5 and 2/5 tiles are refused on the second pick); and two colours meaning 50:50 (the guess slip).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtree is this topic's own mechanism: growing a two-stage tree from a start node, dragging fractions onto six branches, multiplying along a highlighted path and checking it against 200 picks, adding two mixed-colour path ends, then relabelling the second stage when an item is eaten. It is not the spinner-reshape lab of 105 (flagprob), the fair-versus-unfair lab of 920 (flageqlik) or the add-to-one spinner of 857 (flagsumone). The lab-distinct gate keeps it under the 30 percent shingle limit against every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner grows the tree and sees the six listed outcomes before 2 × 3 is written, fills every branch and is told that each pair from one point adds to 1, must choose multiply over add before 9/25 appears and then sees 72 of 200 agree, must pick both mixed paths before 12/25 is shown, and must relabel the second picks out of 4 before 3/5 × 2/4 = 3/10 is written. Wrong tiles and wrong leaves are refused with the reason, so the rule is discovered, then confirmed.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 5 because 2 + 3 (the grown tree lists 6 outcomes); the second-pick chances change even when the counter is put back (they stay 3/5 and 2/5); add along the path (refused because 6/5 is impossible); one path for one of each colour (a second mixed path must be picked); and the second-pick chances stay 3/5 and 2/5 after a sweet is eaten (they become fractions out of 4). The reveal line repeats the learner's own pick against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions, each wrong option tagged with its own slip and a specific message checked in the lab: count (a coin and a dice give 2 × 6 = 12, not 8 or 6), add (do not add along a path), sumone (no rain is 1 − 0.3 = 0.7), replace (after eating a red, 2 of 4 left), onepath (both mixed orders, 12/25) and guess (two colours is not 50:50). Right answers restate the fact with a tick.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text measures FK grade 5.0 against a 6.5 limit, using short sentences and the precise terms in context: tree diagram, branches, path, multiply, add, put back. Adult text is 8.7 against 9.5 and names independent events, sampling with and without replacement, P(A then B) = P(A) × P(B | A) and the law of total probability. Lab labels are short (H, T, R, B, 3/5) and the side panels use one-line equations.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each do one job: what a tree is, branches add to 1, multiply then add, and how not putting back changes the fractions. Adult paragraphs give the formal rules and sources, the named slips, and what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrase and the explanation stays under the 12 percent overlap limit against every lesson, including the earlier probability lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes before and after Show me: the coin-then-spinner tree and its six-outcome list sit side by side with every node and end label readable, the six branch slots and the 3-red 2-blue bag fit with three fraction tiles, the red-red path is a thick purple line with 9/25 and 72 of 200 = 36 percent in the side panel, and the no-putting-back tree shows 2/4, 2/4, 3/4 and 1/4 with P(R,R) = 3/10 under the tree. Nothing is clipped and the buttons stack full width.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Flip the coin, Spin after H and after T, one button per remaining fraction naming the next empty branch, one button per path end, Add versus Multiply, Pick 200 pairs, and one button per path with its probability. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback, right and wrong carry tick and cross marks as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
